answer.says: Ramesh, you ask for what I have not. The state is the actuality of the ethical idea, and the household is its first organ. I have not paid you because I have no money, and I have no money because the state has not recognized me. But the pot is empty because we have not acted. If you go to the shop, you must buy with my money. I have one hundred and sixty-six rupees. Take them. Buy rice, dal, and a little ghee. Do not buy tea. You have tea. The state is not a machine that runs without fuel, and neither is the kitchen. I will write a note for the Directorate tomorrow, but today we must eat. Is that clear?
answer.thought: The tension is simple: I have no cash, he has no goods, and the stove is hot. The ethical idea requires the actual, not the possible. I must give him my last cash to make the household actual, even though it leaves me destitute. It is a dialectic of necessity: my poverty becomes his agency, and his agency becomes my sustenance. I will give him the money and demand food, not luxury. The state is the actuality of the ethical idea, and if the household cannot cook, the state is not actual here.
